neighbours.label: Fires weakly in descriptions of how something is measured or worked out (to calculate the X, to determine X, colonies counted and each traced), not on the same verbs used for personal goals or on narrative sequences.
fire: In this exercise, pupils learn how to calculate the speed of a falling stone.
Engineers used a laser to calculate the exact height of the tower.
Water samples were filtered, and each was weighed to the nearest milligram.
Seeds were planted at three depths to determine germination rates.
The survey team will calculate the area of each field from the photos.
Mutant strains were grown separately and their growth curves compared.
Tree rings were counted to determine the age of the oak.
Students then calculate the volume of the cylinder from its radius.
quiet: In this exercise, pupils learn how to draw a falling stone in pencil.
Engineers used a crane to lift the steel beams onto the tower.
The guests arrived late, and each was given a glass of wine.
Seeds were planted in spring, and the garden looked lovely by June.
The survey team will meet in the village hall after lunch.
The children were grown up and their parents moved to the coast.
The sheep were counted and led back into the barn.
Students then go home on the bus after the last lesson.
